meta.title: Illustrative STPA: landing deceleration
meta.scope: Invented teaching example, not a real aircraft or system. Structure after STPA (Leveson, Engineering a Safer World, 2012; MIT 16.63J notes). Empty UCA cells mean not analysed, not safe.

system.text: Deceleration of an aircraft on the runway after touchdown (invented example)

hazards.text: The aircraft does not decelerate enough to stop within the runway.
hazards.constraint: The aircraft must decelerate to a stop within the runway length.

hazards.text: The aircraft leaves the runway at speed.
hazards.constraint: The aircraft must stay on the runway surface until it is stopped or at taxi speed.

nodes.processModel: Believes the runway is dry and braking will be effective.
Believes the aircraft is on the ground and the wheels are rolling.

nodes.text: Aircraft on the runway (wheels, brakes, spoilers)

actions.text: Arm autobrake and select braking level

ucas.context: After touchdown, with autobrake armed and the runway wet.
ucas.constraint: The controller must apply the brakes after touchdown whenever autobrake is armed.

ucas.context: Autobrake is armed after touchdown instead of before landing.
ucas.constraint: Autobrake must be armed before landing.

ucas.context: Manual braking is released while ground speed is still high.

scenarios.text: The ground-contact signal is not received, so the controller believes the aircraft is still airborne (wrong process model).
